collectible_reason:
Issued by the Central Committee of the National Liberation Front of South Vietnam (the "Viet Cong"), whose name is printed across the front. The notes are dated 1963 but were held back until the fall of Saigon in 1975, when they briefly became the currency of the Provisional Revolutionary Government in the South. They were replaced after reunification in 1978.

They are a short-lived wartime and transition currency and a direct link to the end of the Vietnam War. Uncirculated examples are fairly common today because unissued stocks reached collectors.

title: Whitman Fifty State Quarters folder (1999–2008, P & D)
collectible_reason:
The 50 State Quarters program (1999–2008) issued five new quarter designs a year, one per state, in the order the states joined the Union. It was the most popular coin program in US history. The Mint estimated that over 140 million people collected them, and folders like this Whitman "Deluxe Edition" were how most families did it. This folder has a hole for every state from both the Philadelphia (P) and Denver (D) mints: 100 slots in all.

Circulated state quarters are worth face value or a little more. The fun is in completing the set. A few error coins are worth real money, such as the 2004-D Wisconsin with an "extra leaf" on the corn stalk and the 2005-P Minnesota with a doubled die showing extra trees, so the Wisconsin-D and Minnesota-P slots are worth a look.
notes: Photographed pages: 2002–2004 has 28 of 30 slots filled (missing Arkansas-D and Texas-D); 2005–2007 has 7 of 30 filled (all five 2005-P, Minnesota-D and Nebraska-P). The 1999–2001 and 2008 pages haven't been photographed yet.

collectible_reason:
A **blue-seal silver certificate**: until 1964 this dollar could be exchanged at the Treasury for a dollar's worth of silver, as the wording above Washington's portrait says. Silver certificates stopped being redeemable for silver in 1968, and many people saved them as keepsakes.

Series 1935-D notes were printed in huge numbers, so circulated ones are common and worth a few dollars. Collectors look for **star notes** (a ★ in the serial number), which this one isn't, and the 1935-D "wide" and "narrow" back-design varieties.

title: Kennedy half dollars — binder page A (20 pockets)
collectible_reason:
A full page of Kennedy half dollars: 20 pockets, several with two or more coins stacked. It includes at least four **Bicentennial** halves dated 1776–1976, which show Independence Hall on the back instead of the eagle, plus dates through the 1970s and early 1980s.

Kennedy halves from 1971 on are copper-nickel and worth about face value; people collect them as a date run. The thing to check is the second pocket of the fourth column, which looks brighter and may be dated **1964**. That would make it 90% silver (about $21), and 1965–70 halves are 40% silver (about $8).
